data.gender_notes: Ishira is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ishira is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘Ishana’, meaning god, and ‘Ish’, meaning knowledge or wisdom. The name Ishira symbolizes the goddess Ishani, who is believed to bestow the gift of knowledge upon her devotees. The name Ishira carries the meaning “Goddess Ishani's giver of knowledge” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ishira usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess ishani's giver of knowledge and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Ishira is mentioned in the ancient Sanskrit epic Mahabharata, in the context of the celestial nymphs known as Apsaras. Ishira is said to be the mother of three celestial children, named Tvaastara, Dhruvana and Nabha, who were born from the moon god's (Chandra's) semen that fell onto her body while she was bathing in the river Saraswati. This event occurred during the Dwapara Yuga.

Ishira is also mentioned in the Puranas, particularly in the Agni Purana, as the name of one of the 21 daughters of King Sahasrarjuna of Haihayas. Ishira is described as a beautiful and virtuous princess who was married to King Mandhata, the legendary emperor of Haihayas. This event occurred during the reign of Mandhata, which is believed to be around 2100 BCE.

On Instagram, there are numerous accounts dedicated to the study of Hindu deities, astrology, and spiritual practices, with many featuring the name Ishira in their titles or hashtags. On Pinterest, users can find boards related to Hindu mythology, spirituality, and astrology, with pins featuring images of Ishira or the goddess she is associated with, Goddess Lakshmi. On TikTok, there are videos showcasing the significance of Ishira in Hindu mythology and how it relates to personal growth and astrological signs. Overall, the name Ishira represents a connection to ancient wisdom and spiritual practices, and its modern usage reflects the growing interest in these areas among contemporary audiences.
